result.title: Diff-IrisPAD: Modeling Bona Fide Iris Distributions for Unsupervised Presentation Attack Detection
result.summary: Iris recognition systems are vulnerable to presentation attacks (PAs), including textured contact lenses, print replays, and synthetic irises. Existing PAD methods rely on supervised learning with attack data, limiting generalization to unseen attacks and new sensors. We propose Diff-IrisPAD, an unsupervised framework based on Brownian Bridge Diffusion that models bona fide iris distributions without using attack samples. The method reconstructs clean iris textures from degraded inputs and detects attacks via reconstruction inconsistency using ViT scoring and pixel-level measures. Experiments on a large-scale multi-sensor dataset (125K+ images, NIR and VIS, 8 attack types) show that Diff-IrisPAD achieves an overall ACER of 30.52, significantly outperforming diffusion-based baselines while demonstrating strong generalization to unseen attacks. These results highlight the effectiveness of diffusion-based bona fide modeling for robust and scalable iris PAD.

AI.brief_summary: 提出基于 Brownian Bridge Diffusion 的无监督虹膜呈现攻击检测框架，仅用真实样本建模干净虹膜纹理分布，通过重建不一致性（ViT 评分与像素级度量）识别攻击。
AI.relevance_reason: 属于生物特征安全中的生成式异常检测，缺少推理状态、视觉证据获取与多模态推理环节；重建差异打分虽可用于可靠性判别，但线索过于通用，未见与 LVR 的具体联系。
